title: Strong and weak acids
caption: A strong acid such as HCl is fully ionised in water: every molecule has given its proton to water. A weak acid such as HF ionises only slightly, so most of it stays as molecules and [H₃O⁺] is much lower at the same concentration.
alt: Two beakers: hydrochloric acid with only H₃O⁺ and Cl⁻ ions; hydrofluoric acid mostly as HF molecules with a few H₃O⁺ and F⁻ ions.
description: Hydrochloric acid: 6 H₃O⁺ and 6 Cl⁻, no HCl molecules left.
Hydrofluoric acid: 5 HF molecules and only 1 H₃O⁺ and 1 F⁻.
